9c9c752b1c98538e8feb1c41841409fb47829740.summary: Vendor profile by SOCRadar (published 2024-03-18, updated after July 2025) of ShinyHunters, a cyber threat group the report says first emerged in 2020 and sells or leaks stolen databases, and runs or ran BreachForums. It lists claimed breaches of Tokopedia, Microsoft GitHub, Wattpad, Pixlr, Pizza Hut Australia and AT&T, and a 2025 Salesforce CRM extortion wave that Google tracks as UNC6040. Methods named include phishing, vishing, exposed credentials, unsecured cloud buckets and malicious OAuth apps. Sebastien Raoult was sentenced in Seattle. Most breach figures are claims or allegations.

hedges: Most breaches are described as claimed or alleged by the group; the report does not confirm them.
The Tokopedia data is described as allegedly offered for sale on a dark web market.
The Microsoft GitHub breach is described as reportedly compromising about 500GB, based on the group's own claims.
Pizza Hut Australia did not directly respond; there is no official statement linking the breach to ShinyHunters, though researchers suspect involvement.
AT&T stated its systems had not been compromised. The March 2024 BreachForums post was allegedly from a distinct threat actor.
At the time the CRM attackers' identity was unknown; by July 2025 victims reported extortion emails naming ShinyHunters, suggesting the group's involvement.
The report says it believes the group now operates as a flexible extortion-as-a-service model.
Signs of overlap with Scattered Spider and possibly former Lapsus$ members are described as signs only.

9c0213480f79537a8a176527f2133f7eddc28391.summary: Proofpoint overview of Cobalt Strike, a legitimate penetration-testing tool that threat actors increasingly use. Proofpoint reports a 161 percent rise in threat actor use from 2019 to 2020 and assesses it is increasingly used as an initial access payload. Named users include TA800, TA547, TA415, TA423, TA3546 and APT29. The report says investigators attributed the SolarWinds campaign to threat actors working for Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service.
